question: True or false: some people blind in part of their visual field can still point accurately to objects there?
answer: True. Lawrence Weiskrantz studied a patient, DB, whose damaged visual cortex left him insisting he saw nothing on one side; yet he guessed the position and tilt of lines there far above chance. Weiskrantz called it blindsight. A great deal of what the brain does with information never reaches awareness.
move: Doing something well does not mean you are aware of doing it.
ask: Which of my snap judgements happen without my noticing, and might deserve a slower second look?
trap: False, assuming seeing and knowing you see are the same thing.
reference: Weiskrantz, Blindsight: A Case Study and Implications, Oxford University Press, 1986
